question: The doctor orders Paracetamol 500 mg. Pharmacy sends Paracetamol scored tablets of 250 mg each. How many tablets will you give?

options.A: 1 tablet
options.B: 0.5 tablets
options.C: 4 tablets
options.D: 2 tablets

explanation: Using Desired over Have: (500 mg / 250 mg) × 1 tablet = 2 tablets. Perfect!

question: What is the standard rule for turning a bed-bound patient to help prevent pressure sores?

options.A: Every two hours
options.B: Every six hours
options.C: Once per shift
options.D: Only when they complain of pain

explanation: Turning a patient at least every two hours takes the weight off vulnerable spots, giving blood flow a chance to rush back in and save the skin. Simple and life-saving! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)

question: How should numbers inside a research table column normally be aligned?

options.A: To the right or by decimal points
options.B: Centered with uneven spacing
options.C: To the extreme left margin
options.D: Diagonally across the cells

explanation: Right-aligning or lining up numbers by their decimal points makes it super easy to compare sizes up and down at a glance.

question: How does the pain of a duodenal ulcer typically behave compared to other stomach discomfort?

options.A: It stays constant all day and never changes with meals
options.B: It gets better after eating food and worsens hours later
options.C: It becomes much worse immediately upon swallowing food
options.D: It only hurts during heavy physical exercise at night

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Food temporarily buffers the stomach acid so you feel relief, but once the stomach empties and acid hits the sore again, the pain returns.

question: A patient taking oral metronidazole complains of stomach upset. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Crush the tablets and mix them into a citrus fruit juice
options.B: Double the next dose to compensate for the upset stomach
options.C: Take the medication with food or milk to ease gastric irritation
options.D: Stop taking the medication immediately and discard the remaining pills

explanation: Correct! Metronidazole can be tough on the tummy, but taking it with meals or milk helps soothe the stomach without losing drug power.

question: A male patient comes to the clinic with a thick yellow discharge from his urethra and burning pain when urinating. What is the most likely culprit?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Acute kidney injury
options.C: Gonococcal urethritis
options.D: Urinary tract bladder stone

explanation: That classic yellow discharge combined with burning urination is a textbook sign of Gonorrhea affecting the urethra.

question: Why do we have to be extra careful and double-check our work when giving injections?

options.A: Oral medications require much higher doses than injections.
options.B: Errors can cause rapid and severe harm because absorption is direct.
options.C: Hospital insurance policies mandate double-checking every dose.
options.D: The digestive system neutralizes all injectable substances.

explanation: Spot on! Once a drug is inside the body via injection, you can't take it back out. That's why accuracy is super important.

question: How does water move from inside the gut into the bloodstream during oral rehydration?

options.A: It follows sodium and glucose passively via osmosis
options.B: It is pumped across by high-pressure gradients
options.C: It travels through separate channels unaffected by solutes
options.D: It is pushed across by active muscular contractions

explanation: Water loves to follow where solutes go! When sodium and glucose are absorbed into the gut cells, water naturally follows them to keep the balance right.

question: A community health nurse wants to protect HIV-negative teens who are at high risk of exposure. Which preventive medication should the nurse discuss?

options.A: Emergency therapeutic surgical procedures
options.B: Intravenous antibiotic loading doses
options.C: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP)
options.D: Immediate lifelong antiretroviral treatment

explanation: Spot on! PrEP involves taking daily anti-HIV medications to significantly lower the chances of catching the virus.

question: Why is rational drug use so important in the fight against antibiotic resistance?

options.A: It ensures that pharmaceutical companies make higher profits annually
options.B: It guarantees that all drugs are manufactured using local herbs only
options.C: It stops patients from ever visiting a public health facility again
options.D: It prevents the overuse and misuse of antibiotics that cause bacteria to mutate

explanation: Spot on! Using antibiotics wisely stops germs from learning how to beat our drugs.

question: A new mother bleeds heavily because a small piece of the placenta was left behind in the uterus. Which of the 4 Ts does this fall under?

options.A: Thrombin
options.B: Tone
options.C: Trauma
options.D: Tissue

explanation: When membranes or pieces of the placenta stay behind inside, we group that under 'Tissue'. Making sure the placenta is complete upon delivery prevents this!

question: What causes foot drop in bedridden patients who don't get proper nursing support?

options.A: Wearing compression stockings that are too tight
options.B: Walking too much on hard hospital floors without shoes
options.C: Drinking too little water during daytime shifts
options.D: Leaving the feet unsupported in plantar flexion for too long

explanation: When toes point downward unsupported for days, the calf muscles and Achilles tendon tighten up permanently. Simple foot supports easily prevent this!

question: Which of these is a non-pharmacological (drug-free) way to help manage labor pain?

options.A: inhalation of nitrous oxide gas
options.B: hydrotherapy and massage
options.C: continuous epidural anesthesia
options.D: intravenous opioid administration

explanation: Correct! Warm water baths (hydrotherapy) and massage are wonderful, drug-free comfort measures for laboring mothers.

question: Which of these actions is a dangerous nursing practice that you must strictly avoid after giving an injection?

options.A: Engaging built-in safety shields
options.B: Throwing away syringes immediately
options.C: Using a sharps container
options.D: Recapping used needles by hand

explanation: Spot on! Trying to recap needles by hand is a major cause of accidental needle-stick injuries. Never do it!

question: What is NOT a typical challenge faced by disease surveillance systems in developing settings?

options.A: Delays in transporting clinical samples due to poor roads
options.B: An overabundance of fully staffed reference laboratories
options.C: Inadequate funding for rapid response outbreak teams
options.D: Poor reporting compliance by overburdened health workers

explanation: A lack of laboratories and equipment is a major challenge, not an overabundance of them. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h7)

question: During a home visit, what is a key sign of neglect that a community health nurse should look for?

options.A: Frequent attendance at youth club meetings
options.B: A high grade point average in primary school
options.C: Poor hygiene and delayed physical growth milestones
options.D: Excessive participation in neighborhood sports

explanation: Physical signs like poor hygiene and stunted growth point directly to a lack of proper care, food, and supervision at home. Excellent assessment skill to master!

question: Why do bedridden patients often need extra protein in their diet?

options.A: Bed rest causes the body to sweat out all available amino acids
options.B: Dietary protein replaces the need for physical therapy exercises
options.C: Illness and immobility trigger a state that breaks down muscle
options.D: Proteins are needed to lubricate the moving joints directly

explanation: Being stuck in bed puts the body in a breakdown state (catabolism) where muscle is lost faster. Extra protein helps fight off this muscle wasting!

question: Which hormone is produced by the placenta to help maintain the corpus luteum and pregnancy in the early stages?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.D: Thyroid-stimulating hormone

explanation: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is secreted early in pregnancy to signal the corpus luteum to keep producing progesterone until the placenta takes over. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h7)

question: Why do cystine stones form much faster when the urine is acidic?

options.A: Acidic conditions accelerate the speed of the glomerular filtration rate
options.B: Low pH causes the kidneys to manufacture more amino acids
options.C: Cystine has very poor solubility at a low pH level
options.D: Acidic urine destroys the protective lining of the renal pelvis

explanation: Cystine doesn't like to dissolve in acid! When urine is acidic, cystine clumps together instead of staying dissolved, turning into stubborn little crystals and stones.

question: What vital document must a nurse provide when sending a client to another facility?

options.A: A receipt for the purchase of family planning drugs
options.B: A discharge certificate from the local government
options.C: A blank prescription sheet signed by the patient
options.D: A completed and legible referral form

explanation: A formal referral form communicates the clinical history and reason for transfer directly to the receiving healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h5)

question: What happens to blood vessels when you apply a cold compress?

options.A: Vasoconstriction
options.B: Capillary rupture
options.C: Aneurysm formation
options.D: Vasodilation

explanation: Cold makes blood vessels narrow down (vasoconstriction), which slows down blood flow to the area and stops swelling from getting out of hand.

question: Why is there a small balloon near the tip of an indwelling urinary catheter?

options.A: To open up a blocked urethral passage
options.B: To measure the pressure inside the bladder
options.C: To hold the catheter securely inside the bladder
options.D: To prevent bacteria from traveling up the tube

explanation: Great job! Once water goes into that tiny balloon, it acts like an anchor so the tube stays safely put without slipping out.

question: How is the role of a nurse in assisted living different from a nurse in a busy hospital?

options.A: Assisted living nurses focus more on wellness, supervision, and chronic care coordination.
options.B: Acute care nurses have no responsibility for monitoring patient vital signs.
options.C: Assisted living nurses provide continuous one-on-one surgical recovery care.
options.D: Acute care nurses never supervise nursing assistants.

explanation: Spot on! While hospital nurses handle unstable, emergency conditions, assisted living nurses focus on long-term wellness, chronic care, and guiding support staff.

question: What is the main goal of a negative feedback loop in the body?

options.A: To trigger rapid nerve impulses during acute physical pain
options.B: To maintain hormone levels within a stable, normal range
options.C: To continuously amplify hormone production until exhaustion
options.D: To replace lost nutrients in the extracellular fluid

explanation: Think of negative feedback like an air conditioner: when the room gets too cold (or hormone levels get too high), it turns things off to keep balance.

question: What is one of the main duties of a community health nurse regarding occupational safety?

options.A: Educating workers on hazard recognition and protective gear
options.B: Designing industrial machinery for manufacturing companies
options.C: Enforcing labor laws through police intervention
options.D: Managing the financial accounts of private factories

explanation: Community nurses shine at health education—teaching everyday workers how to spot dangers and use protective gear correctly.

question: Why must a chest drainage system always be placed lower than the patient's chest?

options.A: To make it easier for the patient to walk around the unit
options.B: To ensure the water seal chamber bubbles continuously
options.C: To use gravity to keep fluid draining away from the pleural cavity
options.D: To prevent the suction regulator from breaking

explanation: You nailed it! Gravity is our helper here; keeping the canister low ensures fluid drains out of the chest and doesn't flow back in.

question: During which weather condition or season do cerebrospinal meningitis outbreaks typically peak in northern Nigeria?

options.A: Throughout heavy coastal rainfall
options.B: During the dry harmattan season
options.C: During periods of extreme flooding
options.D: In the middle of the humid summer

explanation: Dry, dusty harmattan winds irritate the upper respiratory lining, making it easier for bacteria to invade and cause meningitis. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h3)

question: A confused elderly patient is admitted to the ward. Which temperature route is safest and most appropriate for initial assessment?

options.A: Axillary or tympanic
options.B: Sublingual
options.C: Rectal
options.D: Oral

explanation: Confused patients cannot safely hold a thermometer in their mouth or cooperate with rectal insertion, making non-invasive routes much safer. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why do surgeons often tie and heat-seal the tubes during a vasectomy?

options.A: To prevent the cut ends from spontaneously reconnecting
options.B: To completely numb the scrotal sac for pain relief
options.C: To speed up the healing of the outer scrotal skin
options.D: To destroy any remaining sperm inside the testicles

explanation: Spot on! Using two methods like tying and sealing ensures the tubes don't accidentally grow back together.

question: How can poor food storage at home harm a child's health?

options.A: It lowers the market price of local vegetables.
options.B: It reduces the child's daily physical activity levels.
options.C: It automatically increases the vitamin content of stored grains.
options.D: It causes foodborne infections that trigger diarrhea and hinder nutrient absorption.

explanation: Spot on! Spoiled or contaminated food leads to tummy infections, making it hard for the child's body to keep the nutrients it needs.

question: Why is a quick chat with a patient at the bedside considered health education?

options.A: Every clinical interaction is an opportunity to share knowledge
options.B: Patients prefer talking over reading heavy medical textbooks
options.C: Hospital management requires a daily quota of conversations
options.D: It gives the nurse a break from heavy physical tasks

explanation: Exactly! Teaching doesn't only happen in a formal classroom. Even a brief chat while checking vitals helps a patient understand their health better.

question: When would you expect to see bladder irrigation actually ordered for a patient?

options.A: Mild urinary incontinence in an elderly resident
options.B: A routine change of a long-term Foley catheter
options.C: Gross hematuria with active blood clot formation
options.D: Uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection symptoms

explanation: When heavy blood and clots start blocking the catheter, irrigation is the go-to fix to clear the tube and get things moving again.

question: Why is the role of a food handler particularly critical in a hospital environment?

options.A: Hospital patients eat more frequently than people outside
options.B: Hospital kitchens prepare larger quantities of food than standard restaurants
options.C: Hospital patients often have weakened immune systems that make them vulnerable to infections
options.D: Hospital food handlers are required to have medical degrees

explanation: Vulnerable patients in healthcare facilities suffer severe complications from foodborne illnesses that healthy people might overcome easily. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h2)

question: What does two-way communication mean in a referral system?

options.A: The ambulance driver talks directly with the hospital gatekeeper
options.B: The family calls the clinic every morning and evening
options.C: Information goes to the hospital and feedback returns to the clinic
options.D: The patient speaks to both the doctor and the nurse at the same time

explanation: Two-way communication ensures the referring nurse learns what happened to the patient and how to manage them during follow-up. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h3)

question: What is the normal, healthy look of a newly made intestinal stoma?

options.A: Pink to brick-red
options.B: Bright yellow or green
options.C: Dark purple to black
options.D: Pale white or gray

explanation: Correct! A healthy stoma is packed with tiny blood vessels, which gives it a nice moist, pink to brick-red color.

question: What is the main reason for nursing supervision in the hospital ward?

options.A: To ensure care meets safe and ethical standards
options.B: To discipline staff who make clinical errors
options.C: To reduce the number of working hours for nurses
options.D: To replace formal classroom nursing education

explanation: Think of supervision as a supportive guide. Its main job is to make sure patient care stays safe, proper, and of high quality!

question: What is the final step after completing a thorough research critique?

options.A: Firing staff members who do not read journals
options.B: Writing a textbook about research methods
options.C: Throwing away the article because all studies have flaws
options.D: Deciding whether the evidence is strong enough to change clinical practice

explanation: The ultimate purpose of nursing research critique is to determine if and how the findings can safely improve patient care. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is a common research duty for a bedside staff nurse?

options.A: Collecting data and identifying study participants
options.B: Funding major multi-center clinical drug trials
options.C: Writing national health policy legislation
options.D: Publishing textbooks for medical schools

explanation: Bedside nurses are closest to patients, making them well-suited to spot eligible participants and gather accurate clinical data. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h2)

question: A patient stays home from work, complains of body aches to their partner, and rests in bed. Which stage of illness behavior is this?

options.A: Dependent client role
options.B: Assuming the sick role
options.C: Recovery stage
options.D: Medical care contact stage

explanation: Spot on! At this stage, the person accepts that they are sick, gets support from loved ones, and takes a break from their normal daily duties.

question: Why do nurses pinch the skin when giving a subcutaneous injection to a slim patient?

options.A: To squeeze out trapped air bubbles inside the syringe
options.B: To speed up the absorption of the medication into blood
options.C: To lift the fatty tissue away from the underlying muscle
options.D: To numb the nerve endings near the injection site

explanation: Pinching gathers up that cozy layer of fat and safely lifts it away from the muscle underneath, ensuring your needle goes exactly where it's supposed to.

question: What is the main characteristic of a Schedule I controlled substance?

options.A: High potential for abuse and no accepted medical use
options.B: Used only in emergency rooms for sudden cardiac arrest
options.C: Low risk of addiction and available over-the-counter
options.D: Safe enough to be given without any professional oversight

explanation: Schedule I drugs have the highest abuse potential and are not approved for standard medical treatment. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h4)

question: A patient tells you they only want a general idea of their condition and do not want all the technical details. What is the most appropriate nursing response?

options.A: Tell their family members the full medical report instead
options.B: Insist they hear everything so they can make informed choices
options.C: Respect their preference and provide a clear, high-level summary
options.D: Refuse to talk to them until they agree to hear all test results

explanation: Patients have the right to guide how much information they receive, and nurses should honor these individual preferences. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is the bioavailability of a medication given directly through an intravenous (IV) line?

options.A: 10 percent
options.B: 100 percent
options.C: 50 percent
options.D: 0 percent

explanation: Because IV meds go straight into your veins, they bypass the gut and liver completely. That means 100% of the dose reaches your bloodstream instantly!

question: What does social inclusion in healthcare mean for everyday patients?

options.A: Ensuring everyone can access essential health services without discrimination
options.B: Providing free medications to every citizen in the country
options.C: Requiring all healthcare workers to speak multiple local languages
options.D: Building larger hospitals in urban centers to accommodate more patients

explanation: Spot on! Social inclusion is all about making sure every person gets fair access to health services without facing unfair barriers or bias.

question: At what point in an illness can a patient usually start receiving palliative care?

options.A: Only during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.B: At the time of a serious illness diagnosis
options.C: Only when admitted to a dedicated hospice facility
options.D: After all curative treatments have completely failed

explanation: You don't have to wait until the end! Palliative care is meant to start early alongside other treatments to keep the patient as comfortable as possible.

question: What is the main job of barium sulfate during a lower GI X-ray?

options.A: Lubricate the rectal wall to ease tube insertion
options.B: Act as a contrast medium that blocks X-rays so the bowel shows up clearly
options.C: Stimulate rapid peristalsis and empty the colon
options.D: Absorb excess gas pockets inside the large bowel

explanation: Barium sulfate is a special metallic compound that X-rays cannot easily pass through. This makes the lining of the bowel stand out brightly on the image!

question: When a baby's head is nicely tucked with the chin to the chest, what is the measurement of the suboccipito-bregmatic diameter?

options.D: 9.5 cm

explanation: When the baby tucks its chin right into its chest, it presents its smallest and best measurement for birth: 9.5 centimeters. Beautiful design by nature!

question: Which finding in a jaundiced newborn must be reported immediately because it points to bile duct disease?

options.A: Frequent crying during diaper changes
options.B: Clay-colored or pale stools
options.C: Yellow skin extending to the toes
options.D: Mild sleepiness between scheduled feeds

explanation: Stools that look pale or clay-colored mean bile isn't reaching the gut, which can signal a serious condition like biliary atresia. You are learning to spot the critical details!

question: Why is regular multi-disciplinary follow-up essential for adults living with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: To monitor and manage progressive long-term damage to major body organs
options.B: To perform routine blood transfusions that reverse the abnormal gene sequence
options.C: To prevent the patient from ever experiencing another painful crisis again
options.D: To ensure the patient takes daily antibiotics to cure the genetic mutation

explanation: Chronic organ damage to the kidneys, lungs, brain, and joints accumulates over years, requiring coordinated specialist care to catch and treat complications early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h8)

question: Why is it dangerous to just silence an infusion pump alarm and walk away?

options.A: Unresolved alarms cause the pump to reverse fluid flow into the bag
options.B: It can delay necessary treatment or fail to catch a dangerous blockage
options.C: Hospital policy fines staff members who touch alarms too quickly
options.D: The pump will automatically erase all patient data if silenced

explanation: You got it! Alarms are there for a reason. Ignoring them without fixing the root cause can leave your patient without their meds or miss a serious line problem.

question: A husband accompanies his pregnant wife to antenatal care. What should the nurse encourage him to learn?

options.A: Counsel other couples in the waiting room.
options.B: Learn about pregnancy danger signs and birth preparedness.
options.C: Perform a physical abdominal examination on his wife.
options.D: Prescribe prenatal vitamins to prevent anemia.

explanation: Teaching partners about warning signs ensures they can act quickly if an emergency happens. Wonderful!

question: Why is preventing diseases just as important as treating sick patients in the community?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any medications or hospitals
options.B: It ensures that doctors only work during morning hours
options.C: It stops illnesses before they spread and overwhelms the health system
options.D: It removes the responsibility of health from the individual person

explanation: Prevention saves lives and keeps our clinics from getting completely overwhelmed. Stopping trouble early is always a win!

question: Why must physical patient registers and folders be locked away in storage cabinets when not in use?

options.A: It stops government auditors from reviewing financial records.
options.B: It protects sensitive client information from unauthorized access and maintains privacy.
options.C: It ensures nurses spend more time looking for missing keys.
options.D: It prevents facility rodents from chewing on paper pages.

explanation: Locking records away keeps prying eyes off private medical history and honors our professional duty of confidentiality.

question: At what cervical dilation does the active phase of normal labor officially start on a partograph?

options.A: 8 centimeters
options.B: 10 centimeters
options.C: 1 centimeter
options.D: 4 centimeters

explanation: 4 centimeters is your magic marker! That is where the active phase of labor officially begins on the partograph.

question: Why are spinal reflexes important for the body?

options.A: They allow the brain to store long-term memories of painful events
options.B: They control conscious decisions made during physical exercise
options.C: They circulate nutrients through the spinal canal
options.D: They provide rapid, automatic responses without waiting for brain processing

explanation: Reflexes bypass the brain to react instantly to danger, such as pulling a hand away from a hot stove. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h3)

question: What do we call a non-living object—like a stethoscope, door handle, or bed sheet—that can pass germs from one person to another?

options.A: Reservoir
options.B: Vector
options.C: Carrier
options.D: Fomite

explanation: You've got this! Non-living items that carry germs around are called fomites. Think of things like dirty linens or blood pressure cuffs moving microbes from patient to patient.

question: Why is an anticholinergic drug like atropine given along with neostigmine?

options.A: To make the reversal agent work twice as fast in an emergency
options.B: To keep the patient deeply asleep while the breathing tube is removed
options.C: To prevent dangerous spikes in blood pressure caused by neostigmine
options.D: To counteract unwanted slow heart rate and increased secretions caused by neostigmine

explanation: Neostigmine can cause bradycardia and too much spit or mucus. Atropine steps in to dry things up and keep the heart rate steady!

question: Why do we use standard universal precautions for every single woman admitted to the labor ward?

options.A: Any patient can carry blood-borne infections even if their screening status is unknown
options.B: It saves time by eliminating the need to check laboratory test results
options.C: Pregnant women never develop secondary bacterial infections during birth
options.D: Government regulations only apply infection control to surgical patients

explanation: We treat all body fluids as infectious because in an emergency, we might not know a patient's status yet. Safety first for everyone!

question: What happens during tubular reabsorption in the nephron?

options.A: Urine is pushed down the ureters through muscular contractions
options.B: Extra metabolic wastes are pumped from the blood into the tubule
options.C: Useful substances are moved from the renal tubules back into the blood
options.D: Blood pressure forces large proteins through the glomerular membrane

explanation: Your kidneys filter a lot of good stuff by accident at first! Tubular reabsorption acts like a salvage yard, pulling water, sugar, and nutrients back into your bloodstream.

question: What actually happens during an intrauterine insemination (IUI) procedure?

options.A: A hormonal patch is applied to the abdomen to trigger ovulation
options.B: Mature eggs are harvested directly from the ovaries using a needle
options.C: Fertilized embryos are surgically placed directly into the fallopian tubes
options.D: Washed sperm is placed straight into the uterine cavity using a thin catheter

explanation: You nailed it! IUI helps by placing prepared sperm right inside the uterus, giving them a shorter trip to the egg. Keep it up!

question: What colour and flow pattern does arterial bleeding typically show?

options.A: Bright red and trickling evenly
options.B: Bright red and spurting in jets
options.C: Dark red and oozing slowly
options.D: Dark red and flowing in a steady stream

explanation: Arteries carry oxygenated blood under high pressure from the heart, causing it to spurt out in pulses when a vessel is cut. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h1)

question: Why is looking into a patient's eye with an ophthalmoscope so useful for checking whole-body health?

options.A: The eye mirrors the brain with 100% perfection
options.B: It lets doctors look directly at living tiny blood vessels and nerves
options.C: It is the only organ affected by high blood sugar
options.D: It has the most pain receptors in the body

explanation: Spot on! Because the eye is clear, healthcare workers can peer right inside to see how tiny blood vessels are doing without cutting anything open.

question: Why do women with very short menstrual cycles have a higher chance of developing endometriosis?

options.A: They cause the ovaries to produce abnormal thyroid hormones
options.B: They increase total lifetime exposure to menstruation and estrogen
options.C: They prevent the uterine lining from forming a thick functional layer
options.D: They cause immediate blockage of the cervical os during bleeding

explanation: More frequent periods mean more rounds of retrograde bleeding and hormone exposure over a lifetime, giving the condition more opportunities to develop.

question: Which of these is NOT a common hurdle when setting up reproductive health networks?

options.A: Logistical constraints like poor roads and stock-outs
options.B: Inter-agency rivalry and bureaucratic silos
options.C: Deep-rooted cultural stigma and moral judgment
options.D: Universal access to unlimited financial resources for all clinics

explanation: You got it! Clinics usually struggle with chronic shortages of cash, so having unlimited funds is definitely not a reality or a barrier!

question: How does dehydration often show up first in an older adult?

options.A: Rapid bone density increase
options.B: Excessive weight gain
options.C: High blood pressure spikes
options.D: Sudden onset of confusion

explanation: Surprise! In the elderly, dehydration doesn't just show up as dry skin—it often presents as sudden confusion or acting out of character. Always check hydration first!

question: What is syndromic management of sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Treating infections based on recognized groups of symptoms when lab tests are unavailable
options.B: Isolating infected patients in private hospital wards for weeks
options.C: Waiting for definitive blood culture results before starting any medication
options.D: Treating only the male partner in cases of recurrent vaginal discharge

explanation: Syndromic management allows prompt treatment of common STI symptoms during the initial clinic visit using standardized flowcharts. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a good strategy for teaching a patient with an endocrine condition?

options.A: Providing clear written action plans for emergency symptoms
options.B: Tailoring the teaching session to the patient's cultural background
options.C: Giving long medical lectures without checking for understanding
options.D: Using a return-demonstration approach for practical skills

explanation: Correct! Long, boring lectures don't help anyone learn. We always want interactive teaching and plenty of feedback!

question: What is the name of the primary law protecting persons with disabilities in Nigeria?

options.A: The Discrimination against Persons with Disabilities Act
options.B: The Public Infrastructure and Welfare Decree
options.C: The Nigerian Social Services and Rehabilitation Law
options.D: The National Health Insurance Scheme Act

explanation: Passed in 2018, this Act protects the rights of individuals with disabilities and outlaws discrimination in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h2)

question: When should instruments be checked for cleanliness and damage?

options.A: Directly after removal from the autoclave
options.B: Only when the surgeon complains about a tool
options.C: As soon as the items arrive dirty from the ward
options.D: After cleaning and before packaging

explanation: Staff inspect instruments right after they are washed and dried. This ensures no hidden dirt or broken parts slip through before they are wrapped up.

question: What is the primary cause of constipation and heartburn during pregnancy?

options.A: Complete cessation of digestive enzyme production in the stomach
options.B: Rapid over-activity of the bowel wall muscles
options.C: Relaxation of smooth muscle caused by elevated progesterone
options.D: Direct compression of the liver by the growing fetus

explanation: Progesterone slows down peristalsis throughout the gastrointestinal tract and relaxes the sphincter separating the stomach from the esophagus. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h4)

options.D: Positive feedback pushes systems away from normal balance and can cause harm if unchecked

question: Which of these is NOT a common stressor that can worsen anxiety for people living in Nigeria?

options.A: Economic hardship and inflation
options.B: Security challenges and community unrest
options.C: Societal pressures regarding family provision
options.D: Abundant financial surplus and job security

question: Which of these is NOT an ethical requirement during a health screening exercise?

options.A: Keeping client test results strictly confidential

options.D: Explaining the limitations of the screening test

question: What is a major difference between normal postpartum blues and postpartum depression?

options.A: Postpartum blues resolve on their own within two weeks
options.B: Postpartum depression appears on the first day after delivery
options.C: Postpartum depression only affects women who had cesarean births
options.D: Postpartum depression require immediate psychiatric admission

explanation: The 'baby blues' are mild and usually fade away within a couple of weeks without special treatment, whereas postpartum depression is heavier, lasts longer, and needs real support. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h6)

question: What is the main reason we monitor a child's growth at the clinic?

options.A: To detect growth problems before visible signs appear
options.B: To treat children who already have severe infections
options.C: To vaccinate children against common childhood illnesses
options.D: To provide free food supplies to low-income families

explanation: Spotting small changes in weight or height early lets you step in and help before severe malnutrition sets in. You've got this!

question: Why do healthcare organizations use a progressive discipline system?

options.A: To give employees a chance to correct their behavior
options.B: To make sure every minor mistake leads to firing
options.C: To avoid keeping any documentation of employee errors
options.D: To bypass labor laws during staff investigations

explanation: Progressive steps ensure fairness by allowing staff to improve before facing severe penalties like losing their job. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h5)

question: What is a common result when a primary breadwinner develops a disabling chronic illness?

options.A: Automatic government provision of permanent housing
options.B: The complete elimination of domestic chores
options.C: Shifts in household roles and financial responsibilities
options.D: Immediate improvement in overall family communication

explanation: A major illness forces other family members to take over tasks previously managed by the sick individual. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the main difference between an acute kidney injury and chronic renal failure?

options.A: Chronic renal failure always resolves completely with proper hydration therapy.

options.C: Acute injury only affects the bladder, while chronic failure affects the entire ureter.
options.D: Chronic renal failure involves permanent and irreversible loss of nephron function.

question: Which hormone surge directly triggers ovulation around day 14 of the cycle?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: You nailed it! A sudden spike in luteinizing hormone (LH) is the green light that causes the ovary to release a mature egg.

question: In Nigerian reproductive health programs, what does the acronym PMTCT stand for?

options.A: Primary Medical Treatment for Chronic Tumors
options.B: Prevention of Mother-To-Child Transmission
options.C: Public Midwifery Training and Community Testing
options.D: Postnatal Management of Teenage Children and Teens

question: In inflammatory joint conditions, what is 'pannus'?

options.A: An abnormal tissue layer that destroys cartilage and bone
options.B: Fluid accumulation in the outer layer of the skin
options.C: Thickened scar tissue formed after a surgical incision
options.D: A hard calcium crystal deposit inside the joint space

explanation: Pannus is an extra layer of bad, granulation-like tissue that grows inside the joint and slowly eats away at the cartilage and bone. You'll often see this in conditions like rheumatoid arthritis!

question: What is the quickest and most practical way for a nurse to check what a patient has eaten recently during a busy clinic day?

options.A: Admitting the patient for a week
options.B: Testing stool samples for fat
options.C: Asking for a 24-hour dietary recall
options.D: Ordering a full metabolic blood panel

explanation: Spot on! Asking 'What did you eat and drink yesterday?' gives you a fast, reliable picture of their current intake.

question: Your syringe driver beeps with an occlusion alarm. What is the very first thing you should check?

options.A: If the room lights are turned on brightly
options.B: Whether the extension tubing is kinked or clamped
options.C: Whether the pharmacy has new medication orders
options.D: If the patient's blood pressure is stable

question: Which germ is the main cause of Tuberculosis (TB)?

options.A: Staphylococcus aureus
options.B: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.C: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae

explanation: You've got this! TB is caused by a tough germ called Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Knowing your causative agents is key on the wards!

question: Why do nurses need to assist some patients with feeding?

options.A: To ensure adequate nutrition for patients who cannot feed themselves

options.C: To speed up meal times in busy hospital wards
options.D: To test the patient's swallowing reflexes before discharge

explanation: You've got this! Assisted feeding is simply stepping in to help patients who aren't able to eat on their own yet, making sure they get the strength they need.

question: What is the main purpose of a tally sheet during a busy immunization outreach?

options.A: To record the home address and phone number of each mother
options.B: To write detailed medical histories for every child present
options.C: To quickly count services rendered without writing full names
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of the vaccines

explanation: Exactly! Tally sheets let us use quick tick marks to keep track of patient volume during busy clinic hours without slowing down to write long names.

question: What is the best way to wash loose dirt and germs out of a fresh cut?

options.A: Soaking the entire wound in a tub of tap water
options.B: Scrubbing the inside of the cut with dry gauze
options.C: High-pressure irrigation using normal saline

explanation: Using a syringe with sterile saline creates just enough gentle pressure to wash away debris without harming the healing flesh. You're building great clinical skills!

question: Why is it sometimes good if a deworming drug stays in the gut and isn't easily absorbed into the blood?

options.A: It ensures the drug travels directly to the brain tissues
options.B: It prevents the liver from metabolizing any medication
options.C: It reduces the need for patients to drink water

explanation: Makes sense, right? Keeping the drug right in the intestines means it hits the tummy-dwelling worms with full force!

question: What is the main goal of Nigeria's National Reproductive Health Policy and Strategic Framework?

options.A: To reduce high rates of maternal and child mortality
options.B: To replace traditional birth attendants with medical doctors
options.C: To privatize all primary health care centers in the country
options.D: To increase the importation of foreign pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: You've got this! The core aim of this framework is to tackle the heavy burden of maternal and child deaths through coordinated health actions.

question: Why is it important to pick the right statistical test for your research data?

options.A: Patients will refuse to take their medications if the math is wrong
options.B: Ethical boards will fine the nursing unit for messy spreadsheets
options.C: Using the wrong test can lead to false conclusions and bad clinical practices
options.D: Hospital computers will crash if you select an improper formula

explanation: Right on target. Different questions need different math tools; using the wrong one gives misleading answers that could affect patient care.

question: What are the three essential parts of a strong advocacy message?

options.A: The history, the theory, and the research
options.B: The problem, the solution, and the urgency
options.C: The budget, the timeline, and the penalty
options.D: The diagnosis, the drug, and the dosage

explanation: Keep it simple and clear: state what is broken, how to fix it, and why we need to act right now!

question: Why are grab bars installed in bathrooms for individuals with physical disabilities?

options.A: To block water from splashing onto the bathroom floor tiles

options.C: To serve as hanging storage for lightweight assistive devices

question: Why is it helpful for the body to use direct nerve control during sudden danger?

options.A: It relies entirely on blood nutrient concentration changes

options.C: It provides a much faster response than hormonal feedback loops

explanation: When danger strikes, you don't have time to wait for slow chemical travel—nerves act in a split second to keep you safe!

question: Why would a nurse need to provide alternative ways for a patient to pass urine or stool?

options.A: The patient is unable to walk to the toilet independently
options.B: The hospital policy requires all bedridden patients to use bedpans
options.C: It reduces the total amount of daily nursing documentation
options.D: It completely prevents any risk of a hospital-acquired infection

question: About how long does one full sleep cycle (moving through NREM and REM stages) last?

options.A: 90 to 110 minutes
options.B: 30 to 45 minutes
options.C: 3 to 4 hours
options.D: 6 to 8 hours

explanation: Your brain cycles through different sleep stages roughly every hour and a half all night long.

question: What happens to bile between meals when your body doesn't need it right away?

options.A: It is filtered out by the kidneys and eliminated in urine

options.C: It is stored and concentrated inside the gallbladder
options.D: It is sent back to the stomach to digest proteins

explanation: When you're not eating, your gallbladder acts like a storage pouch, holding onto bile and thickening it up until you eat something fatty and it's time to squeeze it out.

question: A patient with ALS is having muscle weakness and wasting. Which part of the nervous system is mainly affected?

options.A: The myelin sheath of peripheral nerves
options.B: Upper and lower motor neurons
options.C: Dopamine receptors in the basal ganglia
options.D: Sensory nerve endings in the skin

explanation: ALS attacks the motor neurons that tell your muscles to move. When these cells weaken, the muscles waste away (atrophy). You are building fantastic clinical knowledge!

question: What is the typical average length of a complete ovarian cycle?

options.A: 28 days
options.B: 40 days
options.C: 14 days
options.D: 7 days

explanation: A standard text-book ovarian cycle is calculated to last about twenty-eight days, though normal variations among women are very common. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h1)

question: How do nurses best create a supportive clinical environment for FGM survivors?

options.A: By offering empathetic listening, privacy, and non-judgmental care
options.B: By refusing to treat patients who refuse surgery
options.C: By discouraging patients from talking about their pain
options.D: By asking intrusive questions in front of waiting crowds

question: What is the big advantage of giving tumor chemotherapy through an artery instead of a vein?

options.A: It completely eliminates all side effects throughout the entire body
options.B: It delivers a higher concentration of the drug directly to the tumor site
options.C: It prevents the drug from ever entering the systemic circulation
options.D: It allows the patient to take the chemotherapy medication at home

explanation: Think of it like dropping the medicine right on the doorstep of the problem! It gives the tumor a concentrated dose before the blood carries it away.

question: Why do we use skin traction right after a bone fracture?

options.A: To speed up the growth of new skin cells
options.B: To completely eliminate the need for pain medication
options.C: To permanently heal the bone without surgery
options.D: To relieve painful and violent muscle spasms

explanation: Steady pulling tires out the muscles around the break, stopping those painful spasms that pull the bone ends out of place. Keep up the good work!

question: What is a common non-pharmacological comfort measure for a patient suffering from severe itching (pruritus)?

options.A: Applying hot heating pads directly over the itchy rash
options.B: Encouraging the patient to scratch freely with long nails
options.C: Scrubbing the dry skin vigorously with a rough washcloth
options.D: Applying cool compresses to the affected itchy areas

question: A patient is leaving the hospital after treatment for a deep fungal infection. Which oral azole is commonly used for long-term follow-up care?

options.A: Nystatin

options.C: Caspofungin
options.D: Fluconazole

question: Why should a nurse use a tongue depressor or gloved finger rather than bare fingers to scoop cream from a jar?

options.A: To force the cream to bypass the epidermal stratum corneum layer
options.B: To ensure the cream is heated to body temperature before spreading
options.C: To make the medication absorb five times faster into the bloodstream
options.D: To prevent contaminating the entire container of medication with microbes

explanation: Dipping bare hands into a shared medication jar introduces bacteria from the nurse's hands into the product, risking infection for future applications. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h7)

question: What does 'silent hypoxia' mean in COVID-19 patients?

options.A: A complete absence of lung sounds during stethoscope auscultation
options.B: Normal breathing rates paired with severe panic attacks
options.C: Elevated carbon dioxide levels despite normal oxygen saturation
options.D: Dangerously low blood oxygen levels without the feeling of breathlessness

question: What is the main purpose of denial when a patient first gets bad news?

question: A patient has a critically high potassium level. Which emergency medication combo helps push potassium out of the blood and back into the cells?

options.C: Normal saline and potassium chloride

question: What is considered the most reliable indicator of a patient's pain intensity?

options.A: The nurse's clinical observation of vital signs

options.C: The family member's estimate of the discomfort
options.D: The patient's personal self-report

question: Where do newly formed sperm go right after leaving the walls of the seminiferous tubules?

question: Which symptom is uniquely linked to COVID-19 compared to many other common respiratory infections?

options.A: Loss of taste or smell
options.B: Yellow skin discoloration
options.C: Uncontrollable muscle spasms
options.D: Severe joint stiffness

question: What is the main catch or limitation of chemical buffer systems?

question: A patient with a stroke in the front of the pons is fully awake and alert, but cannot speak or move their body below the neck. What is this called?

question: Why is catching a high-risk pregnancy early so important for us as nurses?

question: What is the difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation requires chemical disinfection of clothing, whereas quarantine requires surgical operations

question: Which leadership style involves sharing decisions and encouraging team input?

question: Which detail is essential to include when charting after suctioning a patient?

question: Which infection is a nurse most afraid of contracting after an accidental needle stick injury?

options.A: Tuberculosis
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Hepatitis B

question: A patient goes home with a PICC line for long-term IV antibiotics. Why use a central line here?

options.C: It allows nurses to directly irrigate the bone marrow every few minutes

question: What structure chemically connects the hypothalamus to the anterior pituitary gland?

options.D: Direct unmyelinated nerve fiber tracks

question: What is the biggest cause of antimicrobial resistance today?

options.A: Misuse and overuse of antimicrobial drugs

options.D: Strict adherence to sterile surgical techniques

question: What should you do with the AED pads if the patient suddenly wakes up and starts breathing?

question: If a patient has a pituitary problem that blocks LH and FSH, what is the most likely result?

question: Which glove material gives you a great feel (tactile sensitivity) but can cause nasty allergies?

question: Where do nurses and midwives primarily interact with the population policy framework?

question: A nurse accidentally pricks a finger with a used needle of unknown status. What is the very first thing to do?

question: Why do nurses use standard screening tools like the Patient Health Questionnaire in clinical practice?

options.A: To quantify and measure depression symptom severity

options.C: To test physical strength and muscular endurance

question: What is the main purpose of continuous monitoring during a BCC project?

question: How is Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) viewed under international human rights law?

options.A: An acceptable alternative traditional medicine practice
options.B: A mandatory cultural initiation rite for minors

question: How do out-of-pocket payment systems negatively affect maternal health?

options.B: They motivate nurses to work longer shifts without resting

question: Why should a nurse focus on health problems that residents care about the most?

options.C: Government regulations legally force citizens to attend health meetings

question: What happens when a healthcare facility fails to maintain proper family planning records?

options.D: Clients automatically stop experiencing contraceptive side effects

question: What is an immediate nursing task to take care of right after an ultrasound scan ends?

options.B: Flush the IV line with heparin

question: Where should the patient stand on the platform during a weight measurement?

question: What is the main job of the countercurrent multiplier in the Loop of Henle?

question: When can palliative care start for a patient with advanced cancer?

question: What is the term for a nurse's legal obligation to answer for their professional actions?

question: Which tiny, hair-like parts of the respiratory tract get paralyzed and destroyed by cigarette smoke?

question: A healthy child receives a routine measles vaccine at the local health clinic. What type of immunity is being stimulated?

options.D: Artificial active immunity

question: What is the main goal of encouraging student self-assessment in nursing education?

options.B: To replace faculty-led clinical evaluations with student opinions.
options.C: To promote critical self-reflection and lifelong professional growth.
options.D: To reduce the workload of clinical instructors entirely.

explanation: Self-assessment helps you look at your own strengths and weaknesses so you can keep growing into an awesome, reflective nurse.

question: What is the best way to explain home care instructions to a patient with low health literacy?

options.A: Relying entirely on written pamphlets without verbal explanation
options.B: Using simple, plain language and asking the client to repeat instructions
options.C: Speaking in complex clinical terminology to sound professional
options.D: Handing the client a dense medical textbook to read overnight

explanation: You got it! Plain words plus the teach-back method (asking them to explain it back to you) guarantees they truly understand their treatment.

question: What is the best way to communicate with a patient experiencing memory issues or confusion?

options.A: Use short, simple sentences and ask one question at a time
options.B: Ask multiple questions at once to save time
options.C: Avoid speaking to the patient and talk only to the wall
options.D: Argue with the patient whenever they become confused

explanation: Keep it brief and sweet! Asking too many things at once can easily overwhelm someone who is dealing with cognitive decline.

question: You are getting ready to repair a perineal tear after delivery. Which drug should you draw up to numb the area?

options.A: Lidocaine
options.B: Hydralazine
options.C: Ergometrine
options.D: Magnesium sulfate

explanation: You got it! Lidocaine is our go-to local anesthetic for numbing the perineum before doing a repair or episiotomy.

question: What is the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in home care?

options.A: Proper hand hygiene
options.B: Restricting all visitors permanently
options.C: Wearing sterile gowns all day
options.D: Spraying rooms with strong perfumes

explanation: Good old-fashioned handwashing is your best defense! It removes germs and stops them from passing between you and your patients.

question: A young woman comes to the clinic with sudden, severe pain on one side of her lower abdomen and vomiting. What condition should the nurse think of first?

options.A: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.B: Follicular cyst rupture
options.C: Ovarian torsion
options.D: Endometriosis flare-up

explanation: Sudden one-sided pain and vomiting are classic red flags for ovarian torsion, where the ovary twists and cuts off its own blood supply. It's a true emergency!

question: What do we mean by the term 'hidden hunger'?

options.A: People hide their food insecurity out of shame in rural communities
options.B: Individuals consume adequate calories but lack essential vitamins and minerals
options.C: Food items lose their nutrients completely during traditional cooking
options.D: Laboratory tests cannot detect nutritional shortages in the early stages

explanation: Spot on! 'Hidden hunger' happens when someone gets enough food to feel full (calories), but their body is starving for vital vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why should a nurse manager figure out the exact type of conflict happening?

options.A: To decide which nurse should be fired
options.B: To punish the staff members involved
options.C: To pinpoint the true source of friction
options.D: To fulfill mandatory hospital paperwork

explanation: Spotting the right category helps leaders fix the actual root cause instead of just treating surface drama. Spot on!

question: Your patient gets an IV antibiotic and suddenly has trouble breathing, swollen lips, and wheezing. What should you grab first?

options.A: Topical hydrocortisone cream
options.B: Intravenous multivitamins
options.C: Oral paracetamol tablets
options.D: Subcutaneous epinephrine

explanation: That's anaphylaxis—a true emergency! Quick epinephrine saves lives by opening up airways and stabilizing blood pressure.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the traditional '5 Ps' of a neurovascular assessment?

options.A: Pulselessness
options.B: Pallor
options.C: Pressure
options.D: Pain

explanation: The standard 5 Ps stand for Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, and Paralysis. Pressure is not one of the five individual assessment items. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is the main difference between a direct and an indirect obstetric death?

options.A: Direct deaths occur during labor, while indirect deaths occur in the postpartum period
options.B: Direct deaths are caused by infections, while indirect deaths are caused by bleeding
options.C: Direct deaths happen in the hospital, while indirect deaths happen at home
options.D: Direct deaths are from pregnancy complications, while indirect deaths are from pre-existing diseases worsened by pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! Direct causes come straight from pregnancy or childbirth issues (like bleeding), while indirect causes happen when a pre-existing condition (like heart disease or malaria) gets worse because of the pregnancy.

question: What type of thinking skills usually show up during middle adolescence?

options.A: Fully mature adult executive reasoning
options.B: Formal operational or abstract thinking
options.C: Pre-operational magical thinking
options.D: Only concrete operational thinking

explanation: Well done! Middle adolescents start thinking beyond what's right in front of them—they can grasp abstract ideas and imagine 'what if' scenarios.

question: Why do blood collection sample tubes come with different colored tops?

options.A: They contain different chemical additives for specific tests
options.B: They indicate the date the tubes were manufactured
options.C: They show which department ordered the laboratory test
options.D: They represent the different sizes of the patient's veins

explanation: Those color codes are lifesavers! They tell you which additive (like anticoagulants or clot activators) is inside for specific lab investigations.

question: Why do nurse educators love using scenario-based multiple-choice questions instead of plain memorization questions?

options.A: They eliminate the need to teach pathophysiology in the classroom.
options.B: They test higher-order thinking and application rather than just memorization.
options.C: They ensure every student achieves a passing grade automatically.
options.D: They take significantly less time for students to read and answer.

explanation: Scenario questions challenge you to think like a real nurse handling a patient situation, which is way more practical than just cramming definitions!

question: Why would an educator use parallel forms reliability for a student exam?

options.A: To eliminate the need for statistical software like SPSS during analysis
options.B: To ensure patients do not experience physical fatigue during long interviews
options.C: To prevent students from copying answers by using two equivalent test versions
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of printing paper questionnaires in the hospital

explanation: Having two fair, equivalent versions of a test lets you switch up questions between rows in a crowded hall without sacrificing test quality!

question: Which signs and symptoms usually show up first when a person is coming down with Ebola?

options.A: Sudden fever, fatigue, and severe muscle aches
options.B: Profuse internal bleeding and skin bruising
options.C: Paralysis of the lower limbs and blindness
options.D: Productive cough and severe chest congestion

explanation: You nailed it! Early Ebola can easily feel like malaria or typhoid at first—sudden fever and body weakness are the major clues.

question: Which of these substances can interfere with platelet function and raise a patient's risk of bleeding?

options.A: Inhaled medications for mild asthma
options.B: Prescribed eye drops for glaucoma
options.C: Herbal supplements like garlic and ginkgo
options.D: Standard daily multivitamins with calcium

explanation: Some common herbal supplements act like natural blood thinners. Always ask patients about herbs and supplements they take at home!

question: How do rigid gender norms typically affect men's health-seeking behaviors?

options.A: They force men to openly share all their vulnerabilities with healthcare providers
options.B: They have zero impact on how men interact with the healthcare system
options.C: They may discourage men from seeking help for emotional or physical pain
options.D: They always encourage men to visit the clinic for routine wellness checks

explanation: Traditional masculine norms often promote self-reliance and stoicism, which can prevent men from reporting symptoms or seeking timely medical care. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is a serious pregnancy danger sign that a mum must report right away?

options.A: Severe headache with blurred vision
options.B: Mild fatigue after moderate housework
options.C: Light swelling of the feet at the end of the day
options.D: Occasional mild heartburn after meals

explanation: A pounding headache and blurry eyes are huge red flags for preeclampsia. Catching this early prevents dangerous seizures!

question: Why can checking a patient's blood composition tell us so much about their overall health?

options.A: Blood circulates through every organ system and directly reflects whole-body health
options.B: Blood pressure remains completely constant regardless of any underlying organ damage
options.C: Blood cells are the largest cells in the human body and easily visible under basic light
options.D: Blood is the only fluid in the body that contains water and dissolved electrolytes

explanation: Spot on! Because blood travels everywhere, it picks up waste and drops off nutrients in every organ. Looking at blood work is like checking the report card for the entire body.

question: Which temperature route gives the closest measurement of the body's core temperature?

options.A: Tympanic
options.B: Rectal
options.C: Axillary
options.D: Oral

explanation: Because it's taken inside the body cavity, a rectal reading is the most accurate reflection of true core temperature. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h2)

question: What happens when you give an opioid antagonist like naloxone?

options.A: It slows down digestion to increase drug absorption.
options.B: It blocks and reverses opioid receptor activity completely.
options.C: It lowers body temperature during a severe fever.
options.D: It stimulates mu receptors to provide deep pain relief.

explanation: Think of naloxone as the ultimate rescue drug. It kicks opioids right off their receptors to instantly reverse dangerous breathing slowdowns.

question: A nurse gives an injection to stop heavy bleeding right after delivery. Which BEmOC signal function is this?

options.A: Execution of assisted vaginal delivery
options.B: Provision of parenteral anticonvulsants
options.C: Administration of parenteral oxytocics
options.D: Manual removal of retained placenta

explanation: Spot on! Uterotonics like oxytocin are injectable drugs used to contract the uterus and stop postpartum bleeding. A key BEmOC skill!

question: What is a key feature of positive discipline?

options.A: Personal accountability and mutual respect
options.B: Heavy financial fines for minor errors
options.C: Strict reliance on fear and threats
options.D: Immediate suspension without investigation

explanation: Positive discipline encourages workers to take responsibility for their actions through cooperation. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h2)

question: What attitude is most essential for a nurse when assessing a patient with a history of FGM?

options.A: Paternalistic and authoritative
options.B: Skeptical and questioning
options.C: Non-judgmental and culturally sensitive
options.D: Indifferent and strictly clinical

explanation: Patients require a safe, empathetic environment free from moral judgment to discuss sensitive genital trauma openly. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a direct complication of an unsafe or incomplete abortion?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Intrauterine adhesions
options.C: Severe pelvic infection
options.D: Heavy hemorrhage

explanation: Gestational diabetes is linked to metabolic changes during an ongoing pregnancy, whereas bleeding, infection, and adhesions follow abortion complications.

question: What is the main reason nurses use fluorescein sodium eye drops?

options.A: To dilate the pupil for a deep retinal view
options.B: To kill bacteria causing severe pink eye
options.C: To highlight scratches and foreign objects on the cornea under special light
options.D: To numb the surface before checking eye pressure

explanation: Fluorescein is a brilliant diagnostic tool! It clings to damaged spots on the cornea and glows bright green under a blue light so you can easily spot tiny scratches.

question: Why would a nurse need to flush or irrigate a patient's ear?

options.A: To drain excessive fluid from the middle ear cavity
options.B: To remove stuck earwax or small foreign objects
options.C: To repair a torn eardrum using pressurized water
options.D: To treat an active bacterial infection deep in the inner ear

explanation: Ear irrigation is a safe way to wash out stubborn wax buildup or little things that got stuck in the outer ear. Great clinical thinking!

question: A newly delivered mother wants to take very hot baths to wash away her postpartum discharge (lochia). What key safety point should you share with her?

options.A: Hot water completely stops the normal production of breast milk
options.B: Heat causes vasodilation, which can potentially worsen postpartum bleeding
options.C: Heat causes immediate permanent blindness in newborns
options.D: Hot water freezes the uterine muscles, preventing involution

explanation: Remember, heat opens up blood vessels (vasodilation). For a new mum, this extra blood flow can actually cause her to bleed more than normal after delivery.

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe nursing action after a patient returns from an MRI where they received mild sedation for anxiety?

options.A: Keeping the hospital bed in a low position with rails up
options.B: Allowing the patient to walk unaccompanied to the bathroom
options.C: Monitoring vital signs until the sedation wears off
options.D: Checking for signs of allergic reactions to any contrast dye

explanation: Sedated patients are at a high risk for falls and dizziness, so they should never walk alone until fully recovered. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h6)

question: Why is watching a patient walk (a gait assessment) so important for nurses?

options.A: It reveals how well the patient balances while moving and indicates fall risk
options.B: It shows whether the patient is digesting food properly
options.C: It measures the exact lung capacity of the patient
options.D: It tests the cranial nerves inside the brain

explanation: Watching how someone walks tells you a lot about their balance and muscle strength, helping you keep them safe from accidental falls.

question: What is a cardiovascular complication?

options.A: A side effect caused by taking too many vitamins
options.B: A normal reaction to doing heavy exercise
options.C: A brand new primary heart disease
options.D: A secondary problem that happens after initial heart or blood vessel damage

explanation: Think of a complication as a follow-up problem. When the heart or blood vessels are already damaged, other issues pop up because the body's normal coping systems get overwhelmed. You've got this!

question: If a needle has a lower gauge number, what does that tell you about its size?

options.A: The needle length is shorter
options.B: The needle width is larger
options.C: The syringe barrel is smaller
options.D: The needle tip is sharper

explanation: Needle gauges can be tricky! Just remember: the smaller the gauge number (like 20G), the thicker and wider the needle is. A higher number (like 25G) is much thinner.

question: A patient arrives at a local primary health clinic with a deep, bleeding wound and signs of shock. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Prescribe mild herbal tea and send the patient away
options.B: Provide first aid, stabilize the wound, and arrange urgent referral to a hospital
options.C: Tell the patient to walk home and rest quietly in bed
options.D: Wait until the next national health campaign day to treat them

explanation: Severe injuries and shock exceed primary clinic capabilities, requiring immediate stabilization and referral to a higher level of care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h8)

question: What do we call the recovery period right after a seizure?

options.A: The permanent damage caused by fits
options.B: The exact moment a seizure begins
options.C: The recovery period right after a seizure
options.D: A test used to diagnose epilepsy

explanation: That phase right after a fit is called the postictal state. The brain is basically resting and resetting, which is why your patient might wake up feeling super tired or confused.

question: Which lab test specifically checks the extrinsic and common pathways of blood clotting?

options.A: Serum electrolyte panel
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Prothrombin Time (PT)
options.D: Blood urea nitrogen

explanation: PT is the go-to lab test to see how quickly the extrinsic pathway and common pathway are getting the job done.

question: Which test is best for looking at soft tissues like a torn knee ligament?

options.A: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.B: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.C: Standard X-ray
options.D: Serum calcium blood test

explanation: MRI uses powerful magnets and radio waves to take clear pictures of soft tissues like ligaments and cartilage. X-rays are great for bones, but MRI wins for soft stuff!

question: What causes painful breast engorgement when a baby misses feeds?

options.A: Sudden permanent damage to the myoepithelial cells
options.B: Accumulation of milk and fluid buildup in the alveoli
options.C: A rapid increase in maternal estrogen levels
options.D: An excessive surge of oxytocin from the posterior pituitary

explanation: Correct! When milk isn't removed, it backs up and causes pressure, swelling, and tenderness in the breast tissue.

question: What is a major complication of untreated chlamydia or gonorrhea in young females?

options.A: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.B: Elevated blood cholesterol
options.C: Chronic juvenile arthritis
options.D: Idiopathic hypertension

explanation: Well done! If lower tract infections are left untreated, they can travel upward and cause painful pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) and fertility issues. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h4)

question: How do cultural food taboos hurt vulnerable groups like pregnant women and young children?

options.A: By forcing them to eat expensive imported foods they cannot afford
options.B: By causing them to drink too much clean water during meals
options.C: By improving their digestion through forced fasting periods
options.D: By restricting nutritious foods and increasing the risk of deficiency diseases

explanation: Spot on. When harmful traditions ban people from eating nutritious things like eggs or meat, vulnerable loved ones miss out on the nutrients they desperately need.

question: Why is it helpful to involve traditional and religious leaders in community health strategies?

options.A: They hold strong influence over community attitudes and can help promote health-seeking behaviors
options.B: They can write legal prescriptions for controlled narcotic medications
options.C: They control the central government budget for foreign medical equipment
options.D: They are legally trained to replace licensed medical doctors in emergency surgery

explanation: Brilliant! Local leaders are deeply respected; partnering with them helps clear up cultural myths and encourages community members to embrace healthcare.

question: A 14-year-old girl is growing fast and has started her monthly periods. How does this affect her food and nutrient needs?

options.A: She only needs extra water and no other dietary changes
options.B: Her nutritional demands decrease because her body is slowing down
options.C: Her nutritional demands remain exactly the same as childhood
options.D: Her nutritional demands increase significantly to support growth and blood loss

explanation: Exactly! Rapid body growth plus monthly blood loss means she needs more energy, protein, and key minerals to stay strong and healthy.
